newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan king undergoes prostate surgery in U.S..
newsitem.headline: Jordan king undergoes prostate surgery in U.S..

text.p: Jordan's King Hussein is recovering at a U.S. hospital after surgery to remove an enlarged prostate that showed no evidence of cancer, doctors said on Saturday.

"His majesty had a benign enlargement of his prostate and we have managed that today...we have studied the tissue on the frozen section and there is no evidence of cancer," U.S. physician Professor Barret, who undertook the operation at Mayo Clinic, Rochester, Minnesota told Jordan television.

The king's personal physician Samir Farraj also told the state television the operation to remove the enlarged part of the monarch's prostate was "100 percent successful" and specimens sent to the laboratory showed no cancerous tumor.
But doctors advised the king, 61, to stay in hospital for a week to be followed by two weeks of recuperation under strict medical observation.
King Hussein started a U.S. visit two weeks ago with a visit to the Mayo clinic he has returned to annually for checkups since surgery for cancer in 1992, with no recurrence of the disease.

The king held a White House meeting last Tuesday in Washington with U.S. President Bill Clinton on the faltering Midde East peace process. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu will visit the monarch in hospital on Sunday.
